source.section: Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules; PDF page 39 Form 540 lines 7 and 9 ('X $153'); PDF page 12 Line 7 and Line 9; PDF page 14 Line 32 and the AGI Limitation Worksheet lines a to i

worked: Married filing jointly, 55 and 52: wages 90,000 and 40,000; federal AGI = 130,000. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 130,000.00. Federal taxable income = 130,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 98,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: none (wages need no adjustment). Form 540 line 14 = 0.00. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 130,000.00 - 0.00 = 130,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (married filing jointly, PDF page 13 chart) 11,412.00. Line 19 taxable income = 130,000.00 - 11,412.00 = 118,588.00. Tax on 118,588.00 by the projection's brackets: 22,158.00 x 1% = 221.58; 30,370.00 x 2% = 607.40; 30,376.00 x 4% = 1,215.04; 32,180.00 x 6% = 1,930.80; 3,504.00 x 8% = 280.32; total 4,255.14. Line 31: Tax Rate Schedule Y (PDF page 75), from its printed base, gives 4,255.14. Line 32 exemption credits: federal AGI 130,000.00 is not more than 504,411.00, so no AGI limitation; line 7 personal 2 x 153 = 306.00; line 9 senior 0 x 153 = 0.00; line 32 = 306.00. Line 33 = 4,255.14 - 306.00 = 3,949.14; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 3,949.14. State income tax = 3,949.14.
